parts.text:
**Medi-Cal** is California’s Medicaid program. It is a public health insurance program that provides free or low-cost medical services for children and adults with limited income and resources. 

Because of major legislative and budget changes at both the federal and state levels, **Medi-Cal is experiencing significant shifts in 2026**. Below is a comprehensive guide to how Medi-Cal works, what is changing this year, and how you can apply.

---

### 1. Key Medi-Cal Changes in 2026
If you are planning to apply or need to renew your coverage, you should be aware of several major policy changes that went into effect on **January 1, 2026**:

* **Reinstatement of the Asset Limit:** 
  * After removing the asset test entirely for a short period (2024–2025), California has **reinstated an asset limit** for non-MAGI applicants (typically adults age 65 and older, people with disabilities, or those in nursing homes). 
  * **The Limits:** The countable asset limit is now **$130,000 for a single person** and **$195,000 for a couple** (plus $65,000 for each additional family member). 
  * *What counts as an asset:* Cash, savings/checking accounts, secondary properties, and extra vehicles. 
  * *What is exempt:* The primary home you live in, one vehicle, personal/household goods, and certain retirement accounts.
* **Immigration Status & Enrollment Freeze:** 
  * Starting January 1, 2026, there is an **enrollment freeze on full-scope Medi-Cal for undocumented adults** (ages 19 and up) who do not have a Satisfactory Immigration Status (SIS). 
  * *Important Exception:* If you were **already enrolled** in full-scope Medi-Cal before December 31, 2025, you will keep your full-scope coverage as long as you complete your annual renewals on time and continue to meet income requirements. If your coverage lapses, you generally cannot re-enroll.
  * Income-eligible children (0–18) and pregnant individuals are **not** affected by this freeze and can still enroll in full-scope Medi-Cal regardless of immigration status.
* **Dental Benefit Reductions (Starting July 1, 2026):** 
  * Adult Medi-Cal members without a satisfactory immigration status (who are grandfathered into full-scope coverage) will lose coverage for routine dental services. Emergency dental care will still be covered for everyone.

---

### 2. General Eligibility Rules & Income Limits
For most adults under 65, pregnant individuals, and families, eligibility is based primarily on your **Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI)**. To qualify for standard MAGI Medi-Cal, your household income must generally be at or below **138% of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL)**. 

**Approximate 2026 Income Thresholds (138% FPL):**
* **1 Person:** $21,597 / year (approx. $1,800 / month)
* **2 People:** $29,187 / year (approx. $2,432 / month)
* **3 People:** $36,777 / year (approx. $3,065 / month)
* **4 People:** $44,367 / year (approx. $3,697 / month)
* *For each additional household member, add $7,590/year.*

*Note: Children in families with incomes up to 266% FPL may qualify for Medi-Cal, and pregnant individuals may qualify with incomes up to 322% FPL through the Medi-Cal Access Program (MCAP).*

---

### 3. What Does Medi-Cal Cover?
Medi-Cal offers comprehensive, "essential health benefits," which include:
* Doctor visits and hospital stays
* Emergency room and urgent care services
* Prescription drugs (through Medi-Cal Rx)
* Mental health and substance use treatment
* Dental services (subject to the July 2026 immigrant adult limitation)
* Vision care (exams and eyeglasses)
* Maternity and newborn care
* Long-term nursing home care and home-based support services
* Non-emergency medical transportation to appointments

---

### 4. How to Apply
You can apply for Medi-Cal year-round (there is no closed enrollment period). There are four primary ways to apply:

1. **Online (Fastest):** You can apply through **[BenefitsCal.com](https://benefitscal.com/)** or **[CoveredCA.com](https://www.coveredca.com/)**. A single application will determine if you qualify for Medi-Cal or a subsidized Covered California health plan.
2. **By Phone:** Call Covered California at **(800) 300-1506** or contact your local county's social services agency.
3. **In-Person:** Visit your local county human services or social services office. (You can find your county office [here](https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/services/medi-cal/Pages/CountyOffices.aspx)).
4. **By Mail:** Download, print, and fill out a paper application from the California Department of Health Care Services (DHCS) website, then mail it to your local county office.
